scope: Same-input local library Fastest search and synthetic watcher comparison; this does not itself prove installed-App behavior or CLI timeout bounds.

aggregation.aggregate: Candidate median / baseline median - 1. Query metrics pool all query iterations; group metrics sum queries within each process, then compare process medians.
aggregation.paired_aba: For each A/B/A block, candidate median / median of the surrounding baseline observations - 1; report both block ratios and their median. Group metrics use whole-process query sums.
aggregation.cpu_gate: code and whole short-suite CPU aggregate and paired medians <= +5%. All individual queries and all blocks are also exposed; a single block exceeding 5% is not silently removed.
aggregation.rss_gate: Engineering review of exact absolute/percentage HWM deltas, with no post-hoc numeric threshold. Capacity must be identical at all instrumented raw memory points.

rss_engineering_review.basis: Exact HWM deltas are reported above; sub-MB / below 0.05% median changes are treated as small sampling/allocator variation, not mathematical zero growth. Packed capacity is independently checked in every short-suite raw memory event.

watcher.limitation: One synthetic A/B/A block lasting about 9 seconds per process; CPU is only about 12 milliseconds per process. This checks event handling and gross resource changes, not long-term idle CPU.

excluded_attempts.reason: Initial driver link failed because the baseline rlib filename did not have the required lib*.rlib form; manifest retained, no measured run events used.

limitations: Two sequential A/B/A blocks per query suite, not a statistical proof or a guarantee for other hardware/data.
The same frozen 7,226,486-record snapshot is used; system caches are not flushed, and each process repeats queries three times. APFS clone copies do not imply a cold physical disk cache.
Child query CPU excludes external RSS sampler CPU; query timers exclude result JSON encoding. Process HWM includes load, search, and result encoding.

RSS phase values use an external 5ms sampler and endpoint/HWM observations; they may miss short peaks or include result encoding. Legacy lower_bound field names are not pure-query allocation guarantees.
Fastest driver has no packed capacity events; the short driver checks the exact same baseline/candidate libraries at load and after every query drop (528 raw points).
No real result records, roots, user paths, database IDs, authentication tokens, or executable paths are exported.
